components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The visually primary action for starting CostCook, emailing Rayan, or booking a demo.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; background: var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); color: #fff; font-family: 'Instrument Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; padding: 1rem 1.75rem; border-radius: 999px; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, transform 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-green-deep, #256549); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: A secondary pill action that stays visibly subordinate beside a filled primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; min-height: 3.25rem; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); border-radius: 999px; background: transparent; padding: 0.9rem 1.5rem; color: var(--color-green-deep, #256549); font-family: 'Instrument Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--color-softgreen, #e5f1ea); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Quiet Action Link
components.description: A secondary action with an expanded 44px touch target, used for phone, sign-in, and contextual contact links.
components.css: .ds-link-quiet { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; color: var(--color-green-deep, #256549); font-family: 'Instrument Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 4px; text-decoration-color: var(--color-hairline, #d3ddd6); transition: text-decoration-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-link-quiet:hover { text-decoration-color: var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); } .ds-link-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: A compact shared navigation destination with a 44px minimum target and quiet default hierarchy.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; color: var(--color-ink-soft, #49524c); font-family: 'Instrument Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: var(--color-ink, #1f2421); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation Disclosure
components.description: A native Resources disclosure for lower-frequency reading and evaluation routes; enhancement only coordinates closure and focus recovery.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-nav-disclosure { position: relative; color: var(--color-ink-soft, #49524c); font-family: 'Instrument Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-nav-disclosure summary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; cursor: pointer; list-style: none; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-disclosure summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; } .ds-nav-disclosure summary:hover { color: var(--color-ink, #1f2421); } .ds-nav-disclosure summary:focus-visible, .ds-nav-disclosure a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-disclosure summary svg { transition: transform 150ms ease-out; } .ds-nav-disclosure[open] summary svg { transform: rotate(180deg); } .ds-nav-disclosure ul { position: absolute; z-index: 1; top: 100%; right: 0; width: 15rem; margin: 0.5rem 0 0; padding: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--color-ticket-rule, #e4d3b4); background: var(--color-paper, #fdfefd); list-style: none; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(31 36 33 / 0.06), 0 10px 28px rgb(31 36 33 / 0.08); } .ds-nav-disclosure a { display: flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-disclosure a:hover { background: #faf5ea; color: var(--color-ink, #1f2421); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-nav-disclosure summary svg { transition: none; } }

components.css: .ds-blog-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 10rem minmax(0, 1fr) auto; gap: 1.5rem; align-items: start; border-top: 1px solid var(--color-hairline, #d3ddd6); padding-block: 1.5rem; color: var(--color-ink, #1f2421); } .ds-blog-meta { display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; color: var(--color-ink-soft, #49524c); font: 600 0.75rem/1.35 'Instrument Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-blog-meta strong { color: var(--color-amber-deep, #8f5716); } .ds-blog-row h2 { margin: 0; font: 600 1.5rem/1.15 'Fraunces Variable', ui-serif, Georgia, serif; } .ds-blog-row h2 a { color: inherit; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: transparent; text-underline-offset: 4px; transition: color 150ms ease-out, text-decoration-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-blog-row h2 a:hover { color: var(--color-green-deep, #256549); text-decoration-color: var(--color-hairline, #d3ddd6); } .ds-blog-row h2 a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-green, #2f7d5b); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-blog-row p { max-width: 65ch; margin: 0.75rem 0 0; color: var(--color-ink-soft, #49524c); font: 400 0.875rem/1.6 'Instrument Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-blog-row time { color: var(--color-ink-soft, #49524c); font: 400 0.75rem/1.35 ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } @media (max-width: 639px) { .ds-blog-row { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 0.75rem; } .ds-blog-meta { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; } }

narrative.overview:
CostCook's incumbent marketing identity is practical, warm, and quiet: an off-white ground, restrained green actions, amber operational accents, and fine rules that recall kitchen tickets without turning the site into a theme. Fraunces gives decisions and page identity an editorial voice; Instrument Sans keeps supporting information direct and easy to scan.

Contact follows the same founder-direct voice. Public visitors get a dedicated /contact destination with email, phone, and demo actions; existing users are directed to authenticated Contact support inside CostCook, where account context can accompany the message.

When marketing needs to show connected product evidence, the same visual world can tighten into a calm, seeded workspace. Editorial Fraunces remains outside and at key explanatory handoffs; dense product labels, tables, statuses, and tabular numbers use Instrument Sans inside a bounded paper surface. This is product proof within the marketing system, not a separate dashboard identity.

Read surfaces extend the ticket into a ruled working notebook. They lead with a real kitchen question, keep arithmetic and assumptions visible, and finish by naming the next operational job. Editorial structure should help a working chef reach a defensible number; it should not turn into a generic publication grid or a product pitch disguised as instruction.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white, green, and amber palette
Fraunces display type paired with Instrument Sans body type
Quiet border rules and sparse, purposeful elevation
Direct actions with explicit outcomes and accessible touch targets
Founder-direct contact language without an anonymous form
Calm, bounded product-proof workspaces with explicit data provenance
Priority-led shared navigation with resilient native disclosures
Question-led read surfaces with visible working and a practical handoff

rules.name: The Quiet Accent Rule
rules.body: Green identifies actions; amber provides small operational emphasis. Neither becomes a broad decorative wash.

rules.name: The Founder-Direct Rule
rules.body: Contact copy speaks as Rayan and names the outcome—email, call, book a demo, or contact support—without invented service guarantees.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Use elevation for physical ticket-like artifacts and bounded product proof, not routine contact information, navigation, or every internal panel.

rules.name: The Prepared-Handoff Rule
rules.body: A static marketing form may prepare a visitor-owned email, but it must distinguish “ready to send” from “sent,” keep the message inspectable in the visitor's email app, and never imply receipt before the visitor sends it.

rules.name: The Priority Ladder Rule
rules.body: Direct links answer the most frequent evaluation questions; grouped links support deeper exploration; quiet account access and distinct demo/start actions retain their own semantic weight.

rules.name: The Native Disclosure Rule
rules.body: Navigation remains complete with JavaScript disabled. Script may improve closure and focus recovery, but never supply the only path to a destination.

rules.name: The Worked-Number Rule
rules.body: Order practical reading as question, arithmetic, boundary or exception, then next job. Keep the calculation and its assumptions visually attached to the decision they support.

rules.name: The Working-Sheet Rule
rules.body: A practical article shows one kitchen question all the way through: formula, bounded example, exceptions, and the next job. Product handoffs follow the instruction; they do not interrupt or masquerade as it.

dos: Do preserve the existing off-white, green, amber, Fraunces, Instrument Sans, and quiet-rule identity when extending contact surfaces.
Do keep public email, phone, and demo actions explicit and outcome-labeled.
Do route existing users to authenticated in-app Contact support.
Do maintain at least a 44px target for the homepage contact action and shared navigation actions.
Do retain the warning against sharing sensitive information.
Do label seeded or constructed product records and amounts as illustrative beside the product proof where the values remain visible.
Do use tabular numerals and quiet rules when presenting operational amounts for comparison.
Do tell visitors when a contact or demo action prepares an email rather than sending data from the site.
Do keep demo and start actions visible and visually distinct when shared navigation condenses.
Do build navigation disclosures on native details and summary, then enhance mutual exclusion and focus recovery.
Do keep Resources as the grouped label for Blog and other lower-frequency reading destinations, with nested resource routes reflected in its active state.
Do keep blog metadata, arithmetic, assumptions, and next-job handoffs visually inspectable with rules, restrained color, and tabular numerals.
donts: Don't add an anonymous public contact form without a new product decision.
Don't invent response-time, availability, or service-level claims.
Don't turn contact guidance into a floating SaaS card or introduce a new visual identity for the route.
Don't present a seeded product workspace as a live account or let decorative dashboard chrome outrank the evidence.
Don't show a sent, received, or confirmed state until the underlying system can prove that state.
Don't flatten every destination, account action, and conversion action into equal-weight header links.
Don't make JavaScript responsible for opening the only route to navigation destinations.
Don't turn practical guides into image-led card grids, decorative hero essays, or product pitches that delay the first useful explanation.
